def: Method explaining history through material conditions and class struggle, insisting the dialectic between imperialism and anti-colonial struggles is central to how the modern world is made. Series Studies on Historical Materialism, n°1.

The study uses 'enslaved' rather than 'slave': the latter can read like a fixed identity; 'enslaved' shows capture, commodification and dehumanisation were imposed, and that slavery did not define the person.
Slavery defined narrowly as chattel slavery (enslaved persons owned as property, transferable); other coerced labour (encomienda, mita) is partly outside scope but part of related history.
Adam Smith calls it originary accumulation; Marx calls 'so-called originary accumulation' expropriation, not accumulation: loot, not savings. Slavery & sugar laid its foundations.

Three-cornered exchange among Europe, Africa and the 'New World': manufactures (incl. Indian textiles, guns, saltpetre) → Africa; enslaved people → Americas/Caribbean; raw materials (sugar, molasses, rum, cotton, silver) → Europe. Other commodities overlooked.
Sven Beckert & Seth Rockman term; plantation system rooted in slavery integrated with credit, insurance, shipping, refining, re-export and finance.
Claude Meillassoux: firearms & gunpowder exchanged for enslaved people ('iron'); sale profit ('gold'); 'production of enslaved people in the womb of iron and gold'.

Licence from the Spanish Crown authorising traders to sell enslaved Africans to Spanish colonies; first 1513; contract; any nationality after 1595; later joint-stock companies; South Sea Company 1713–1739.
Merchant agent managing sale & distribution; 'factor' & 'factorage' older commercial meanings linked to 'factory'; holding, 'seasoning', sorting, credit, risk; skilled & risky business.

term: Real de a ocho (piece of eight)
def: Spanish silver dollar, commodity money equal to its weight in silver; globally accepted; Spain used it to trade with China via the Manila galleon.
Equal-area pseudocylindrical map projection; the study converted its maps from Mercator to Mollweide because 'each projection carries its own ideological bias, Mercator more than others.'

Enslaved people driven in supervised work gangs for long continuous days; gangs by age & capacity (1st/2nd/3rd 'grass gang'); sugar cane + processing integrated. Contrast 'task system' (rice/indigo, US South).
Daily work quota; some time afterwards under strict coercion; common in rice/indigo regions (coastal South Carolina & Georgia); sugar uses gang system.
Sidney Mintz: sugar plantation is 'a synthesis of field and factory'; agricultural production + industrial processing on site; 'human beings as fixed capital... replaceable.'
Portuguese term for sugar mill AND the enslaved people working there; 'as sleepy as an engenho'; church-mandated Sunday/holy-day rest often unhonoured.
Small plots enslaved people worked (e.g. Sundays in Caribbean) to grow own food; without it, plantation diet insufficient.
Third gang: elderly & young children; weeding & gathering grass for animals.
Fibrous cane residue after crushing; used as fuel to boil juice; Barbados practice; Egyptian Mamluk precedent.
Brown, less-refined sugar; 'export of muscovado the more profitable option'; 4× price vs refined in England → transfer pricing; high duties on refined.
Leaving part of cane stalk in soil after harvest to produce a new crop ('vegetative reproduction'); still used.
Unpaid labour peasants owe on lord's land; Mediterranean sugar; replaced/supplemented by enslaved North Africans after Black Death.
Spanish colonial coerced Indigenous labour systems; noted as related history of genocide & coercive labour in the Americas; outside chattel-slavery scope.
Destruction of Indigenous civilisations & social structures in the Americas; false narrative that lands stood empty; land seized; funded plantation expansion; 'genocidal violence'.
Mid-18th to mid-19th c.; conventional narrative airbrushes slavery; sugar refining were 'earliest factory-like workplaces'; predated by slavery-funded capital & reserve currencies.
Immanuel Wallerstein world-systems; Andre Gunder Frank dependency; core/periphery; study emphasises ~500-year configuration, genocide, slavery, colonial plunder.
Global reserve: Spanish dollar → Dutch guilder (Bank of Amsterdam) → British pound sterling → US dollar; rooted in sugar, slavery, silver, asiento; predate Industrial Revolution.
